context_requirements: Active DNA replication (S-phase entry) for replicative polymerase inhibition to cause damage
Intact p53 pathway for robust G1 arrest and apoptosis
Cellular uptake of the inhibitor (many DNA polymerase inhibitors are poorly permeable)
Proliferating cells; quiescent or non-dividing cells will show little response
falsifiers: No change in proliferation or cell-cycle genes at 24 h in any line
No induction of p53 targets (CDKN1A, GADD45A) at 6 or 24 h
Predominant G2/M arrest rather than G1 arrest
No evidence of DNA damage response (no upregulation of repair genes or apoptosis markers)
Strong transcriptional response in non-proliferating HA1E cells comparable to cancer lines

evidence.supports: DNA polymerase inhibition causes G0/G1 arrest in human tumor cell lines
Replicative DNA polymerase inhibitors suppress growth of human cancer cell lines
DNA polymerase inhibitor arrests cells at G1 and induces p53-dependent apoptosis
DNA polymerase inhibition increases DNA damage and induces apoptosis in human colon carcinoma cells
